cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.description: CFB rivalry home dog (LEAD-50): backs the home underdog in a deterministically-identified rivalry-pair game, on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm
cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.notes: Unsigned flag (1 iff a rivalry-pair game AND home is the market underdog, spread_line<0; else 0) on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm. No local rivalry field exists on the CFBD schedule rows (measured: only 3 of 36915 rows mention 'rival' in free-text notes, all one bowl name); rivalry pairs are the deterministic proxy declared in this lane's task -- same team pair met in >=8 consecutive seasons anywhere in the full local schedule history (521 pairs qualify). Disclosed limitation: this captures true historic rivalries (Army-Navy, Auburn-Alabama) but also long-running conference-mandated annual pairings -- no local field disambiguates the two. 4459 rivalry-pair games, 3439 home-underdog games, 1852 flagged (both) of 8933 clean-core games, 0 missing. Positive control +48.405 pts P+ 1.000. Per-era: 2012-2019 +0.037 pts P+ 0.547; 2021-2025 -0.028 pts P+ 0.429 -- both noise-scale (<0.04 pts, P+ within 0.06 of a coin flip), not recorded as separate rows. New family, distinct from the deployed NFL division-revenge overlay and from cfb_rest_bye_replication/cfb_option_prep_screen. Close-graded CFB; no NFL window spent.
cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.plain_summary: Backing the home underdog in a long-running CFB rivalry game is basically a coin flip, tilted very slightly toward working.
